# nish/net/upstream

outbound HTTP/1.1 calls from a route handler that never block its worker: a pool of keep-alive connections to one origin, registered on the `HttpHandler`'s own poll loop and read through the `nish/net/http1-client-codec` codec.

```ts
import {
  UPSTREAM_E_BLOCKED,
  UPSTREAM_E_CLOSED,
  UPSTREAM_E_CONNECT,
  UPSTREAM_E_FULL,
  UPSTREAM_E_LOOKUP,
  UPSTREAM_E_NONE,
  UPSTREAM_E_ORIGIN,
  UPSTREAM_E_REQUEST,
  UPSTREAM_E_RESET,
  UPSTREAM_E_TIMEOUT,
  Upstream,
  UpstreamLimits,
  UpstreamResponse,
} from "nish/net/upstream";
```

<scalar-callout type="info">

```ts
const h = new HttpHandler(new HandlerLimits(), listener, router)
const users = new Upstream(h, "http://127.0.0.1:9000", new UpstreamLimits())
while (true) {
  h.wait(100) // one turn: the handler's sockets and the upstream's
  while (h.ready()) {
    const req = h.take()
    switch (req.route) {
      case USER: if (users.get(req, "/v1/users/7") !== UPSTREAM_E_NONE) { h.problem(req, 503, "Busy", "") } break
      default: h.refuse(req)
    }
  }
  while (users.ready()) { // the answers that arrived this turn
    const r = users.take() // r.req is the request that asked
    if (r.ok) { h.send(r.req, r.status, JSON, r.body, 0, r.length) } else { h.problem(r.req, 502, "Bad Gateway", "") }
    users.release(r)
  }
}
```

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="get returns at once">

It writes the request head into a call slot
taken from a pool, then onto a free connection, or queues it until one is
free, and the program goes on serving. The asking request stays held, as
`nish/net/handler` allows. Each connection is watched on the handler's loop
under a watch id (`UpstreamLimits.firstId` and up), so the program's next
`h.wait` wakes for the upstream as well as for its clients; `ready` then
reads what arrived, once per turn, and hands back every finished call.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Every call ends exactly once, as a call">

A response the codec reads to
its end is `ok` with its `status` and body, whatever the status. Anything
else is `ok === false` with an `error`: one of the codec's `HTTP1_E_`
refusals (a malformed status line, a bare LF, conflicting framing, a body
past `maxBody`, a response cut short), or one of the `UPSTREAM_E_` codes
below (the origin was unusable, the connection failed or closed, the
deadline passed, the path could not be written). The program answers its
own client either way and gives the call back with `release`.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="A kept-alive connection is checked before it is reused">

One the origin
closed or sent bytes on while it was idle is closed instead, so no call is
written to a dead socket or handed bytes it did not ask for. A call the
origin drops unanswered on a reused connection anyway (it closed as the
request crossed) is made once more, on a new connection; a `GET` is safe
to repeat. Two `Upstream`s on one handler must be given watch ids that do
not overlap: nothing checks it, and two with the default limits would both
take ids 8 to 11, each taking the other's wake-ups for its own.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The origin is fixed at start-up">

The constructor parses it, looks its
host up (blocking, once, as a program's start-up may), and keeps one
address; nothing is looked up again, so no later answer can move the pool
somewhere else. When the origin comes from input — configuration, an
environment variable, a request — set `UpstreamLimits.outbound`: the
`nish/net/outbound` policy then checks the host name before the lookup and
the address after it, and a refused origin fails every call with
`UPSTREAM_E_BLOCKED`. Only `http:` is spoken; TLS is not, so `https:` is
`UPSTREAM_E_ORIGIN`.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**Every cap is set at start-up.** The connection count, the call slots
(calls queued, in flight and finished but not yet released), the request
head's room, the response limits the codec enforces, and a deadline per
call. The slots, their head buffers and the connections' read buffers are
made by the constructor; a call's body buffer grows to the largest body it
has held and is kept. Each connection keeps one codec for its life and
the next connection's, reset between them, in its spans mode: a response's
fields are read as spans of a buffer the codec reuses, so a warm pool
allocates nothing per call.

</scalar-callout>

`docs/security/upstream.md` is the record. Private helpers share the
importing program's flat symbol namespace (`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e),
which is why each one carries the module's name.

Written from RFC 9110 and RFC 9112, not ported from another implementation.

## Upstream

A keep-alive pool to one origin, on an `HttpHandler`'s loop.

```ts
class Upstream
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Upstream( h: HttpHandler, origin: string, limits: UpstreamLimits, )` | Parses `origin`, looks its host up once (this blocks for at most `limits.lookupMs`), and makes every slot and connection buffer. Panics when a cap is below 1 or the watch ids run past the handler's. An unusable origin is not a panic: `error` says why, and every call fails with it. |
| `address: u8[]` | The one address the pool connects to, checked against the policy if there is one. |
| `calls: UpstreamResponse[]` |  |
| `connections: UpstreamConnection[]` |  |
| `done: i32[]` | Calls ended and not yet taken, in the order they ended. |
| `doneCount: i32` |  |
| `doneStart: i32` |  |
| `error: i32` | Not `UPSTREAM_E_NONE` when the origin is unusable: every call then fails with it. |
| `errorText: string` | Why the origin is unusable; empty when it is not. For a log. |
| `free: i32[]` |  |
| `freeCount: i32` |  |
| `h: HttpHandler` |  |
| `hostNames: string[]` |  |
| `hostValues: string[]` |  |
| `limits: UpstreamLimits` |  |
| `turn: i64` | The handler turn `pump` last read. |
| `waiting: i32[]` | Calls written into their slot and waiting for a connection, oldest first. |
| `waitingCount: i32` |  |
| `waitingStart: i32` |  |
| `close(c: UpstreamConnection): void` |  |
| `connect(c: UpstreamConnection): void` | Starts a connection for the call `c` holds; a failure ends the call. |
| `dispatch(): void` | Puts waiting calls on connections: a kept-alive one first, then a new one. |
| `end(r: UpstreamResponse, code: i32): void` | Hands `r` to `ready` with `code`. |
| `fail(code: i32, text: string): void` |  |
| `finish(c: UpstreamConnection, code: i32): void` | Ends the call `c` carries with `code`. A connection whose call ended any way but `UPSTREAM_E_NONE` is closed: what is left on it cannot be trusted to start the next response.<br><br>A call that failed on a reused connection before any byte of its response came is not ended but put back at the front of the queue, once: the origin closed the connection as the request crossed it, and a `GET` is safe to send again. Past its deadline it is not. |
| `get(req: HttpRequest, path: string): i32` | Starts `GET path` for `req` and returns at once: `UPSTREAM_E_NONE` when the call is the pool's, which hands it back through `ready` and `take` however it ends; `UPSTREAM_E_FULL` when every slot is taken, and then nothing is held and `req` is still the program's to answer. `path` is copied out before this returns. |
| `idle(): UpstreamConnection \| null` | A connection free for the next call: open, idle and still usable if one is, else closed, else null. An idle connection the origin has closed or sent bytes on is closed here, before a call is put on it. |
| `interest(c: UpstreamConnection, events: i32): void` | Watches `c` for `events` alone. |
| `openConnections(): i32` | How many connections to the origin are open. |
| `parse(c: UpstreamConnection): void` | Takes every event the codec has for the call `c` carries. |
| `pending(): i32` | How many calls hold a slot: queued, in flight, or finished and not yet released. |
| `pump(): void` | Once per handler turn: reads and writes the connections that fired, then fails what is past its deadline. |
| `ready(): boolean` | Whether a finished call is waiting for `take`; reads the upstream's sockets once per handler turn. |
| `receive(c: UpstreamConnection): void` | Reads what arrived and runs the codec over it. |
| `release(r: UpstreamResponse): void` | Gives a taken call's slot back to the pool. Panics for a call not taken or already released: two calls sharing a slot would hand one request's answer to another. |
| `send(c: UpstreamConnection): void` | Writes what the socket takes of the call's head, then waits to read. |
| `service(c: UpstreamConnection): void` | What a connection's turn found ready. |
| `settle(origin: string): void` | Settles the origin: its `Host` value and the one address, or `error`. |
| `take(): UpstreamResponse` | The next finished call, which the program gives back with `release`. Panics when none is `ready`. |
| `usable(c: UpstreamConnection): boolean` | Whether the idle `c` has nothing to read. Anything else closes it: an end of stream or an error means the origin has given it up, and bytes no call asked for would be read as the next call's response. |

## UpstreamLimits

The caps of one `Upstream`, all read once by its constructor.

```ts
class UpstreamLimits
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new UpstreamLimits()` |  |
| `calls: i32` | Call slots: calls queued, in flight, and finished but not yet released, at most. |
| `connections: i32` | Connections to the origin, at most; each takes one handler watch id. |
| `firstId: i32` | The first handler watch id the connections take: they use `firstId` to `firstId + connections - 1`. |
| `lookupMs: i32` | How long the constructor's one lookup of the origin's host may take. |
| `maxBody: i64` | The largest response body the codec accepts, at most 1 GiB; past it the call fails `HTTP1_E_BODY_LIMIT`. |
| `maxHead: i32` | Room for one request head: the request line, `Host` and the empty line. |
| `maxHeaderBytes: i32` |  |
| `maxHeaders: i32` |  |
| `maxStatusLine: i32` |  |
| `maxTrailerBytes: i32` |  |
| `outbound: OutboundPolicy \| null` | Checks the origin's host and address when set; set it whenever the origin comes from input. |
| `timeoutMs: i32` | A call fails `UPSTREAM_E_TIMEOUT` this long after `get` if its response has not ended. |

## UpstreamResponse

One call: the request that asked, then, once `ready` hands it back, how it
ended. The object is the pool's again after `release`.

```ts
class UpstreamResponse
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new UpstreamResponse( index: i32, headRoom: i32, placeholder: HttpRequest, )` |  |
| `body: u8[]` | The body, in `body[0 .. length)`; the buffer is reused, so read `length`, not `body.length`. |
| `deadline: i64` | When the call fails `UPSTREAM_E_TIMEOUT`, on `monotonicNanos`'s clock. |
| `error: i32` | `UPSTREAM_E_NONE`, an `HTTP1_E_` refusal of the codec, or an `UPSTREAM_E_` code. |
| `head: u8[]` | The request head, written by `get`. |
| `headLength: i32` |  |
| `index: i32` |  |
| `length: i32` |  |
| `ok: boolean` | Whether the response was read to its end; `error` says why not. |
| `req: HttpRequest` | The handler's request this call answers. |
| `retried: boolean` | Made once more already, after a reused connection dropped it unanswered. |
| `status: i32` | The final status code, once the response's head has arrived. |
| `taken: boolean` | Taken by the program and not yet released. |

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="34" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`UPSTREAM_E_BLOCKED: i32`

The outbound policy refused the origin's host name or every address it has.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="37" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`UPSTREAM_E_CLOSED: i32`

The connection failed or closed before a response began.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="35" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`UPSTREAM_E_CONNECT: i32`

The connection to the origin could not be made.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="39" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`UPSTREAM_E_FULL: i32`

Every call slot is taken: `get` answers this and holds nothing.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="33" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`UPSTREAM_E_LOOKUP: i32`

The origin's host could not be looked up at start-up.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`UPSTREAM_E_NONE: i32`

The call was read to its end: `ok`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="32" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`UPSTREAM_E_ORIGIN: i32`

The origin is not an `http:` URL with a host and nothing past its authority but `/`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="38" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`UPSTREAM_E_REQUEST: i32`

The path does not start with `/` (an absolute-form or asterisk target is
not this pool's to send), the codec refused to write it, or the head did
not fit `maxHead`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="40" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`UPSTREAM_E_RESET: i32`

The connection failed (it was reset, say) while the response was being read: what came is not the whole of it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="36" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`UPSTREAM_E_TIMEOUT: i32`

The call's deadline passed before its response ended.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
